intro.headline: India in 1930
intro.summary: Highlights of this year's checked items: The Salt March; The Raman effect; Independence Day declared; The first Round Table Conference; The Deccan Queen; B. R. Ambedkar.

technology-science.title: Technology & science
technology-science.standfirst: In this section: The Deccan Queen; State broadcasting begins; The Raman effect; Calculations on a voyage to England.

items.title: The Deccan Queen
items.summary: The Deccan Queen began running on 1 June 1930 between Bombay and Poona. It is described as India's first superfast, long-distance electric-hauled and vestibuled train, with a women-only car and a dining car.

items.title: State broadcasting begins
items.summary: After the private Indian Broadcasting Company went into liquidation on 1 March 1930, the government took over its stations and launched the Indian State Broadcasting Service on 1 April 1930.

items.title: The Raman effect
items.summary: C. V. Raman won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics 'for his work on the scattering of light and for the discovery of the effect named after him'.

sources.label: NobelPrize.org: C. V. Raman, facts (The Nobel Prize in Physics 1930)

items.title: Calculations on a voyage to England
items.summary: On a trip from India to England in 1930, the young physicist Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar worked on the statistics of a degenerate Fermi gas, the start of papers that led to the Chandrasekhar limit for white dwarfs.

specs.label: Service
specs.then: A weekend train with two rakes of seven coaches each (1 June 1930)
specs.now: A daily Mumbai–Pune service run by Central Railway

government-politics.title: Government & politics
government-politics.standfirst: In this section: Viceroy: Lord Irwin; Secretary of State: Wedgwood Benn; The Simon Commission; The first Round Table Conference.

items.title: Viceroy: Lord Irwin
items.summary: Lord Irwin was Viceroy and Governor-General in 1930, the year of the Salt March and the first Round Table Conference.

items.title: Secretary of State: Wedgwood Benn
items.summary: William Wedgwood Benn, a Labour MP, was Secretary of State for India from 7 June 1929 to 24 August 1931.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Secretary of State for India

items.title: The Simon Commission
items.summary: The Indian Statutory Commission, seven British members of Parliament under John Simon, was appointed in November 1927 to review constitutional reform. The Congress and the Muslim League opposed it because it had no Indian member.

items.title: The first Round Table Conference
items.summary: George V opened the conference at the House of Lords on 12 November 1930. Seventy-four delegates came from India, 58 from British India and 16 from princely states, but Congress, whose leaders including Gandhi were in jail, kept away.

items.title: The Sale of Goods Act, 1930
items.summary: The Act, enacted on 1 July 1930 and modelled closely on Britain's Sale of Goods Act 1893, set the law on contracts for the sale of goods across British India.

freedom-history.title: Independence & history
freedom-history.standfirst: In this section: Independence Day declared; The Salt March; The Chittagong armoury raid; Dharasana Salt Works; The Allahabad Address.

items.title: Independence Day declared
items.summary: The Congress asked people to observe 26 January 1930 as Independence Day, after its Lahore session under Jawaharlal Nehru adopted the goal of complete independence.

items.title: The Salt March
items.summary: Gandhi and 78 others set out from Sabarmati on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on the Gujarat coast on 6 April, a 24-day march against the salt tax.

items.title: The Chittagong armoury raid
items.summary: On 18 April 1930 revolutionaries led by Surya Sen attempted to raid the police and auxiliary-force armouries at Chittagong.

sensitivity.note: Armed attack and its aftermath, including executions.

items.title: Dharasana Salt Works
items.summary: On 21 May 1930 satyagrahis led by Sarojini Naidu marched on the Dharasana Salt Works and were beaten by police; the journalist Webb Miller reported 320 wounded.

items.title: The Allahabad Address
items.summary: Muhammad Iqbal, as president of the All-India Muslim League's 21st session, spoke at Allahabad on 29 December 1930.

items.title: The Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha
items.summary: C. Rajagopalachari led about a hundred volunteers some 240 km from Trichinopoly to Vedaranyam, arriving on 28 April and breaking the salt law on 30 April 1930.

personalities.title: Famous personalities
personalities.standfirst: In this section: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi; Jawaharlal Nehru; C. V. Raman; Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar; Surya Sen.

items.title: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi
items.summary: Born in Porbandar in 1869.
items.whyThisYear: He led the Salt March in March and April 1930 and was arrested on 4-5 May.

items.title: Jawaharlal Nehru
items.summary: Born in Allahabad in 1889.
items.whyThisYear: He presided over the Lahore session whose resolution was followed by the 26 January 1930 Independence Day pledge.

items.title: C. V. Raman
items.summary: Physicist, born in 1888.
items.whyThisYear: He won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics.

sources.label: NobelPrize.org: C. V. Raman, facts (The Nobel Prize in Physics 1930)

items.title: Surya Sen
items.summary: Revolutionary, born in 1894.
items.whyThisYear: He led the Chittagong armoury raid on 18 April 1930.

items.title: Muhammad Iqbal
items.summary: Poet and philosopher, born in 1877.
items.whyThisYear: He delivered the Allahabad Address on 29 December 1930.

items.title: B. R. Ambedkar
items.summary: Jurist and reformer, born in 1891.
items.whyThisYear: He was a delegate for the Depressed Classes at the first Round Table Conference and launched the Kalaram Temple movement.

items.title: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay
items.summary: Freedom fighter, organiser and later a champion of Indian handicrafts and theatre.
items.whyThisYear: Gandhi named her one of seven to lead the Salt Satyagraha; she prepared salt on the Bombay beachfront and asked a magistrate whether he would buy her 'Freedom Salt'.

sources.label: Scroll.in: How Mumbai suburban women contributed to the freedom struggle

items.title: Sarojini Naidu
items.summary: Poet and political leader, later the first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress.
items.whyThisYear: After Gandhi's arrest on 4 May 1930 she led the continuing protest at the Dharasana Salt Works on 21 May.

sports.standfirst: In this section: Duleepsinhji's 333 for Sussex; A 2,562-run season.

items.title: Duleepsinhji's 333 for Sussex
items.summary: K. S. Duleepsinhji made 333 in a single day against Northamptonshire in the 1930 English season, still the highest score by a Sussex batter.
items.competition: English County Championship, Sussex v Northamptonshire

items.title: A 2,562-run season
items.summary: Duleepsinhji scored 2,562 runs at an average of 56.93 in 48 innings in the 1930 English season, with nine centuries.

items.title: Duleepsinhji's 173 at Lord's
items.summary: In June 1930 K. S. Duleepsinhji scored 173, his highest Test score, for England against Australia at Lord's.

music-arts.title: Music & arts
music-arts.standfirst: In this section: Gauhar Jaan dies; Nandalal Bose at Santiniketan; Madan Theatres at its peak.

items.title: Gauhar Jaan dies
items.summary: Gauhar Jaan, known as the 'gramophone girl' and India's first celebrity singer, died in January 1930. She had been among the first to record on 78 rpm discs in India, around 1902.
items.creator: Gauhar Jaan

items.title: Nandalal Bose at Santiniketan
items.summary: Nandalal Bose, a pupil of Abanindranath Tagore, was principal of Kala Bhavan at Santiniketan from 1921 and painted scenes from mythology, women and village life.
items.creator: Nandalal Bose

items.title: Madan Theatres at its peak
items.summary: By the late 1920s Madan Theatres owned 127 theatres and controlled half of the country's box office.
